newsitem.title: USA: Procter & Gamble to buy Tambrands -WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Procter & Gamble to buy Tambrands -WSJ.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co is set to to acquire Tambrands Inc for $50 per share or nearly $2 billion, the Wall Street Journal said in Wednesday's electronic edition, citing people familiar with the matter.
The acquisition, expected to be announced today, would be the biggest ever for giant U.S. consumer products company Procter & Gamble, the newspaper said.
Procter & Gamble would also assume Tambrands's debt, the Journal said.
Tambrands shares and options have risen in the past few days on takeover speculation.
The stock closed up 5/8 on Tuesday at 46-1/8, while Procter's stock finished off 1-3/8 at 115-7/8.

On Tuesday, the New York Stock Exchange said Tambrands declined to comment on unusual market activity or takeover rumours. The exchange said it contacted Tambrands "in view of the unusual market activity" in its stock.
Neither company was immediately available to comment on the report, but the Journal said the Cincinnati-based Procter scheduled an analysts' conference call for Wednesday at 0830 EDT/1330 GMT.
Tampax tampons was Tambrands's only surviving product, the Journal said.
A Procter & Gamble spokesman was quoted in the newspaper as declining to comment on the report.
